note: Minutes of a change of station, as assumed in model/nordest.py (CHANGE_METRO): today 20 walking, 20 on the metro or RER, 17.5 waiting; inside one station 5 walking and 7.5 waiting. The split of today's walking between the two stations is for illustration. The script rescales these so that each row adds up to the model's figure. The platform cases give the standing time of a train; the rule (stop, clearing time, share of the hour used) is read from the model.

platform_cases.label: Stops and goes on
platform_cases.note: A TGV stop takes 3 minutes, 4 to 5 at the largest stations. This study counts {stop}.

platform_cases.label: Turns round at a terminal
platform_cases.note: A planning figure of the track owner (then Réseau ferré de France, now SNCF Réseau) for a train reversing at a platform of the Roissy airport station: 20 minutes, called comfortable.

platform_cases.label: Quickest low-cost turn-round
platform_cases.note: The shortest turn-round in the timetable of the low-cost TGV service, which is built on quick turn-rounds: 26 minutes.

platform_cases.label: Terminal turn-round with its margin
platform_cases.note: The same planning figure with the margin kept behind the train: 20 minutes plus about 10. At that standing time the rule gives about one train an hour on each track, which is what Montparnasse delivers today.
